reasoning: Roofline reports compute bottleneck with Compute SOL 92.8% vs Memory SOL 42.1%. Kernel metrics match: sm__throughput is 92.77% of peak sustained, while dram throughput is only 42.12%, so additional speedup must come from reducing instruction cost / improving math efficiency rather than increasing memory bandwidth.

root_causes.cause: Heavy FP32 VALU instruction pressure from explicit reductions and nonlinear ops (sigmoid/exp) dominates cycles.

evidence.interpretation: Very high vector-ALU instruction count indicates arithmetic pipeline is the primary limiter.

fixes.fix: Reduce FP32 math work by using lower-precision accumulation where tolerable (e.g., bf16/fp16 for parts of gate/up or activation path) and/or approximate sigmoid (faster polynomial/fast-math exp).
fixes.rationale: Lower per-element instruction cost on VALU directly targets the saturated compute pipeline.

root_causes.cause: Kernel structure computes 10 independent output blocks (acc0..acc9) in one program, creating large instruction footprint and repeated dot/reduction sequences per j0 iteration.

evidence.interpretation: Large dynamic instruction count suggests instruction throughput/latency is a key bottleneck.

fixes.fix: Retile work to process fewer output blocks per program instance (e.g., split GROUP_N or reduce BLOCK_OUT*GROUP_N fusion), then autotune num_warps/num_stages for the new tile.
fixes.rationale: Shrinking per-program instruction stream can improve scheduler efficiency and reduce compute pressure while maintaining occupancy.
